title: Power Automate for desktop: flowchart mode for building and viewing desktop flows
summary: Hold for an incorrect description of the governance documentation: its Copilot controls are tenant settings or a Microsoft Support request, not Windows registry settings. The roadmap facts, maker controls and absence of a documented flowchart-specific admin switch are supported.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode lets makers build, view and edit desktop flows in Power Automate for desktop.
claims.quote: Flowchart mode introduces a new visual authoring experience in Power Automate for desktop that allows makers to create, view, and edit desktop flows using a flowchart representation.

claims.claim: The maker creation path is Power Automate for desktop: Console > New flow > Create a flow > Flowchart mode (Preview).
claims.quote: Open Power Automate for desktop. In the console, select New flow. In the Create a flow dialog, enter a name for the desktop flow. If you leave the field empty, a name is generated automatically. Select Flowchart mode (Preview).

claims.claim: No API is documented for choosing a desktop flow's designer mode.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop flowchart mode API Dataverse workflow table designer mode. Opened desktop-flow-public-apis and workflow entity reference; searched the reference for flowchart, sequence, designer, visual and ClientData. No mode-setting operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls

claims.claim: The governance page's Windows registry settings do not name flowchart mode.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop flowchart mode disable registry tenant environment admin switch. Opened and read the entire Governance in Power Automate for desktop page, including all registry tables; none names flowchart mode.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode displays actions as nodes on a canvas.
claims.quote: Flowchart mode displays actions as connected nodes on a canvas.

claims.claim: Edges connecting the nodes show execution paths.
claims.quote: Each action is represented as a node, and edges connect the nodes to show their execution paths.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the view can make branches, loops and complex logic easier to understand.
claims.quote: This view can make execution paths easier to understand, especially in flows that contain branches, loops, or other complex logic.

claims.claim: Changes made in one mode are available in the other.
claims.quote: Changes that you make in one mode are available when you open the flow in the other mode.

claims.claim: The new-flow dialog labels the option Flowchart mode (Preview).
claims.quote: Select Flowchart mode (Preview).

claims.claim: An existing flow opened in the designer can switch to flowchart mode through View > Flowchart mode.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An existing flow opened in the designer can switch to sequence mode through View > Sequence mode.
claims.quote: Open the desktop flow in the designer. Select View. To open the flow in sequence mode, select Sequence mode.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Errors must be resolved before switching modes, specifically before switching to flowchart mode.
claims.quote: You can switch to flowchart mode only when the flow has no errors. If the flow contains errors, resolve them before you switch modes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The If action uses a consolidated properties dialog in flowchart mode.
claims.quote: In flowchart mode, the If action uses a consolidated properties dialog that contains the complete conditional structure.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Switch action uses a consolidated properties dialog in flowchart mode.
claims.quote: In flowchart mode, the Switch action uses a consolidated properties dialog for the Switch expression and its cases.

claims.claim: Loop nodes show a loop-back edge representing the loop body.
claims.quote: A loop node has a loop-back edge that represents the loop body and an outgoing edge that continues execution after the loop finishes.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode has a minimap.
claims.quote: The minimap displays a compact overview of the flowchart and identifies the visible area of the canvas.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode supports zoom.
claims.quote: Hold Ctrl and rotate the mouse wheel to zoom in or out.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode supports keyboard shortcuts.
claims.quote: The following keyboard shortcuts apply to canvas navigation and node operations in flowchart mode.

claims.claim: Run from here runs the flow starting from the selected action.
claims.quote: Open a node's context menu and select Run from here to run the flow starting from that action.

claims.claim: Microsoft presents flowchart debugging as using the standard desktop flow debugging tools.
claims.quote: Use the standard desktop flow debugging tools while viewing the flow as a flowchart.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode is documented as a preview feature.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature. Preview features aren't meant for production use and might have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that preview features might have restricted functionality.
claims.quote: Preview features aren't meant for production use and might have restricted functionality.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature is gradually rolling out across regions and may not yet be available in a maker's region.
claims.quote: This feature is being gradually rolled out across regions and might not be available yet in your region.

claims.claim: Flowchart node indexes match sequence-mode action indexes.
claims.quote: Node index badges match the action indexes you see in sequence mode.

claims.claim: Adding an action from an edge inserts the action before opening its properties dialog.
claims.quote: The action is added to the flow before its properties dialog opens.

claims.claim: Closing the properties dialog does not remove the inserted action.
claims.quote: Closing or canceling the dialog doesn't remove the action from the flow.

claims.claim: Move changes a node's visual position without changing execution order.
claims.quote: Moving a node changes only its visual position. It doesn't change the flow's execution order.

claims.claim: Reorder changes execution order.
claims.quote: Reordering a node changes its position in the flow's execution order.

claims.claim: Move and Reorder have different keyboard shortcuts.
claims.quote: The Ctrl+Shift+Arrow shortcuts change only the node's position on the canvas. The Shift+Alt+Arrow shortcuts change the flow's execution order.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Flowchart mode changes authoring and visualization of the same flow rather than introducing a separate runtime flow.
claims.quote: Both modes represent the same desktop flow. Flowchart mode changes how you visualize and edit the current subflow. You still have access to other designer capabilities.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe flowchart mode being applied automatically to existing flows without the maker's choice.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop flowchart mode disable registry tenant environment admin switch; Power Automate flowchart mode switch sequence mode errors restriction. Opened flowchart-flow-designer and governance. Existing-flow switching is documented as a maker action, not automatic.

claims.claim: The governance page lists registry settings restricting sign-in.
claims.quote: Use the following registry entry to keep users from signing in to Power Automate for desktop using a Microsoft account.

claims.claim: The governance page lists registry settings controlling updates.
claims.quote: Use the following registry entry to prevent users from manually updating Power Automate for desktop and receiving update notifications.

claims.claim: The governance page lists registry settings for proxy configuration.
claims.quote: IT administrators can set the following registry key to configure how Power Automate interacts with a corporate proxy server.

claims.claim: The governance page lists registry settings for logging.
claims.quote: Use the following registry entry to configure whether local Power Automate Desktop Designer runs store their action logs on the local machine.

claims.claim: The governance page lists Windows registry settings for Copilot capabilities.
claims.quote: To prevent your users from using any copilot capability contact Microsoft Customer Support to disable all copilot functionality in your tenant.
claims.fix: Remove 'and copilot capabilities' from the list of registry-controlled areas. Replace that sentence with: 'At the time of writing (November 2026), the Learn page on governance in Power Automate for desktop lists registry settings for sign-in, updates, proxy and logging, and none names flowchart mode.' The cited governance page documents Copilot controls through tenant settings or Microsoft Customer Support, not registry entries.

claims.claim: Existing registry settings can restrict access to Power Automate for desktop as a whole.
claims.quote: If all the following registry keys are set to 1, users can't sign in to Power Automate for desktop using any type of account.

claims.claim: Action-based conditions such as If process and If file exists retain their standard properties dialogs.
claims.quote: Action-based conditions, such as If process and If file exists, continue to use their standard properties dialogs.
